rituals.vibeLine: No mission statement. Somehow civilisation continued.
rituals.hook: For one minute, your life is officially off duty from being profound.
rituals.predict: Guess what will go wrong if the next sixty seconds achieve absolutely nothing important.
rituals.play: Do one harmless purposeless thing: look at a spoon, straighten a cushion, stare out a window, doodle a shape. No lesson, no optimisation.
rituals.catch: Check whether meaninglessness for sixty seconds actually damaged anything.
rituals.reveal: The pressure to make every moment matter can become heavier than the moment itself.
rituals.mindBend: Your life can matter without every minute submitting a purpose statement.

rituals.name: THREE MEANINGS, SAME EVENT
rituals.title: THREE MEANINGS, SAME EVENT
rituals.targetPattern: Single fixed meaning assigned to an event
rituals.target_pattern: Single fixed meaning assigned to an event
rituals.precise_subpattern: Single fixed meaning assigned to an event
rituals.vibeLine: Same event. Your brain brought a wardrobe.
rituals.hook: Same event. Three meanings. Let’s see which part is actually glued to reality.
rituals.predict: Guess whether you can make the event mean three different things without changing what happened.
rituals.play: Give the event three interpretations: one harsh, one boring, one unexpectedly generous. Don’t decide which is true yet.
rituals.catch: Notice that the facts stayed still while the emotional meaning moved.
rituals.reveal: Meaning is often constructed after the event, not delivered inside it.
rituals.mindBend: Events happen once. Meaning can be edited more than once.
rituals.ritualCard:
Same event. Three meanings. Let’s see which part is actually glued to reality.
Give the event three interpretations: one harsh, one boring, one unexpectedly generous. Don’t decide which is true yet.
Guess whether you can make the event mean three different things without changing what happened.
Notice that the facts stayed still while the emotional meaning moved. Meaning is often constructed after the event, not delivered inside it.

rituals.vibeLine: Your mood was trying to update your passport.

rituals.title: TINY ENOUGH TO MATTER
rituals.targetPattern: Belief that meaningful action must be large
rituals.target_pattern: Belief that meaningful action must be large
rituals.precise_subpattern: Belief that meaningful action must be large
rituals.vibeLine: Your value does not require a cinematic montage.
rituals.hook: Pick something so small your ambition feels mildly insulted.
rituals.predict: Guess whether a thirty-second action can still count as living a value.
rituals.play: Choose one value—care, courage, learning, honesty, health, creativity. Do the smallest visible action that matches it in under 30 sec.
rituals.catch: Check whether the action becomes meaningless merely because it was tiny.
rituals.reveal: Values describe direction, not minimum order size.
rituals.mindBend: A compass still works when you only take one step.

rituals.vibeLine: Apparently this rule has been freeloading since Year 8.
rituals.hook: Some rules are alive only because nobody held the funeral.
rituals.predict: Guess where this rule came from before you decide whether it still belongs to you.
rituals.play: Write the rule: “I must…” Under it, write the earliest place you remember learning it—family, school, culture, job, one person, or nowhere clear. Add: “Useful then because… Useful now because…”.
rituals.catch: Check if the rule still has a current job or only an old origin story.
rituals.reveal: A rule can be inherited without being chosen.
rituals.mindBend: Old instructions can expire even when they were once useful.

rituals.name: BORROWED GOAL DETECTOR
rituals.title: BORROWED GOAL DETECTOR
rituals.targetPattern: Goals driven by imagined approval
rituals.target_pattern: Goals driven by imagined approval
rituals.precise_subpattern: Goals driven by imagined approval
rituals.vibeLine: Take away the applause and see what is actually yours.
rituals.hook: Let’s check whether this goal is yours or merely renting space in your calendar.
rituals.predict: Guess whose reaction matters most if you imagine quitting the goal tomorrow.
rituals.play: Imagine quietly stopping. Who appears first in your mind looking disappointed, impressed, confused or relieved? Name them. Ask what you would still want if nobody ever found out.
rituals.catch: Notice the gap between the audience goal and the private goal.
rituals.reveal: Approval can power a goal without making the goal personally meaningful.
rituals.mindBend: If nobody could clap, what would still be worth doing?

cheeky.mindBend: If nobody could clap, what would still be worth doing?

rituals.name: TROPHY DISAPPEARING ACT
rituals.title: TROPHY DISAPPEARING ACT
rituals.targetPattern: Worth tied to external markers
rituals.target_pattern: Worth tied to external markers
rituals.precise_subpattern: Worth tied to external markers
rituals.vibeLine: Your certificate vanished. Your actual skill did not get the memo.
rituals.hook: Imagine the trophy vanishes overnight.
rituals.predict: Guess which parts of the achievement survive after the title, certificate, likes or status disappear.
rituals.play: Name the external marker. Now mentally delete it. List three things that remain in you: skill, knowledge, relationship, stamina, choice, story, discipline.
rituals.catch: Check if the achievement becomes literally zero when the symbol is removed.
rituals.reveal: Symbols can vanish faster than the capacities built while chasing them.
rituals.mindBend: The trophy is removable. What it trained in you may not be.

rituals.vibeLine: “More” was hoping nobody asked where it planned to stop.
rituals.hook: If “more” has no finish line, it can run forever.
rituals.predict: Guess the exact point where more money, praise, checking, achievement or certainty would stop noticeably changing today.

rituals.catch: Watch for diminishing returns hiding behind the word “more.”
rituals.reveal: Without a stopping rule, desire keeps moving the goalpost after every win.
rituals.mindBend: Enough is not giving up. It is choosing where “more” stops owning the scoreboard.

Finish five fragments: “I notice… I care about… I’m curious about… I tend to… I’m learning…” Avoid every role label.
Guess whether you can describe yourself for twenty seconds without using a title.
Notice how much self remains when the résumé disappears. Roles organise life, but they are not the full inventory of a person.
↻ INTRODUCE YOURSELF WITHOUT TITLES

rituals.name: REGRET COMPASS FLIP
rituals.title: REGRET COMPASS FLIP
rituals.targetPattern: Short-term fear obscuring longer-term regret
rituals.target_pattern: Short-term fear obscuring longer-term regret
rituals.precise_subpattern: Short-term fear obscuring longer-term regret
rituals.vibeLine: Fear wants comfort now. Future-you may file a complaint.
rituals.hook: Instead of asking “What feels safest now?”
rituals.predict: Guess which future regret feels heavier: trying imperfectly or avoiding completely.
rituals.play: Imagine tomorrow night. Play two ten-second endings: you took the smallest reasonable step, or you avoided it. Which ending leaves less residue?
rituals.catch: Check if fear and regret point in the same direction or different ones.
rituals.reveal: Short-term relief and long-term alignment often vote differently.
rituals.mindBend: Fear asks what hurts least now. Regret sometimes reveals what matters later.

rituals.name: THE INVISIBLE VERSION
rituals.title: THE INVISIBLE VERSION
rituals.targetPattern: A goal surviving only because it is visible to others
rituals.target_pattern: A goal surviving only because it is visible to others
rituals.precise_subpattern: A goal surviving only because it is visible to others
rituals.vibeLine: No applause, no LinkedIn, no gold star. Still want it?
rituals.hook: Let’s make the goal invisible and see if you still want it.
rituals.predict: Guess whether desire goes up, down, or stays the same if nobody will ever know you achieved it.
rituals.play: Picture completing the goal perfectly—but no post, no praise, no title, no one finds out. Sit with that version for 10 sec.
rituals.catch: Notice what happens to the pull of the goal when visibility is removed.
rituals.reveal: Recognition can be part of a goal without being the same thing as wanting the goal.
rituals.mindBend: What remains desirable in private is useful information about what is actually yours.

rituals.targetPattern: Past investment keeping an unwanted goal alive
rituals.target_pattern: Past investment keeping an unwanted goal alive
rituals.precise_subpattern: Past investment keeping an unwanted goal alive
rituals.vibeLine: Past-you can keep the souvenir; present-you does not need the membership.
rituals.hook: Some goals deserve progress.
rituals.predict: Pick one stubborn goal. Guess whether you would choose it today if you had never started it.
rituals.play: Imagine the goal behind museum glass labelled: “Important to me from ____ to ____.” Now ask whether you want to take it home again—or simply respect that it mattered then.
rituals.catch: Check if ending the goal feels less like failure when its past value is preserved.
rituals.reveal: A goal can have been meaningful without needing to remain active forever.
rituals.mindBend: Retiring a goal does not erase the person who once needed it.

jolly.play: Imagine the goal behind museum glass labelled: “Important to me from ____ to ____.” Now ask whether you want to take it home again—or simply respect that it mattered then.
jolly.catch: Check if ending the goal feels less like failure when its past value is preserved.
jolly.reveal: A goal can have been meaningful without needing to remain active forever.
jolly.mindBend: Retiring a goal does not erase the person who once needed it.
jolly.safety:
PAUSE

jolly.theoryBackbone: Sunk-cost effects; goal disengagement; identity continuity

rituals.precise_subpattern: Belief leisure must justify itself
rituals.vibeLine: Your productivity manager is sweating over a doodle.
rituals.hook: For one minute, usefulness is banned.
rituals.predict: Guess how uncomfortable it feels to do something tiny that produces nothing.
rituals.play: Choose one harmless, pointless act: draw a spiral, balance a pen, watch a cloud, make a ridiculous doodle. Do it for 20 sec without turning it into a productivity hack.
rituals.catch: Catch the part of your mind trying to explain why this is secretly useful.
rituals.reveal: A life organised only around utility can turn rest into another performance.
rituals.mindBend: Not everything valuable needs to produce evidence of value.

rituals.title: VALUE WITH A SMALL PRICE TAG
rituals.ritual_name: VALUE WITH A SMALL PRICE TAG
rituals.displayName: VALUE WITH A SMALL PRICE TAG
rituals.targetPattern: Stated values versus revealed willingness
rituals.target_pattern: Stated values versus revealed willingness
rituals.precise_subpattern: Stated values versus revealed willingness
rituals.vibeLine: Beautiful principle. Let’s see if it survives a mildly annoying Tuesday.
rituals.hook: Values sound beautiful when they are free.
rituals.predict: Pick a value you claim matters. Guess one small inconvenience you would willingly accept for it today.
rituals.play: Choose a cost under five minutes, five dollars, or one awkward sentence that supports that value. Don’t do it yet—just notice whether you genuinely want to pay.
rituals.catch: Compare the value you say matters with the cost you are willing to tolerate.
rituals.reveal: Values become clearer when they meet friction.
rituals.mindBend: What matters is not only what you admire; it is what you are willing to inconvenience yourself for.

rituals.vibeLine: No leaderboard. Weirdly, some things still matter.

rituals.catch: Notice which motivations survive the blackout.
rituals.reveal: Scoreboards are useful for measurement, but terrible at explaining why something matters.
rituals.mindBend: A number can track a life without defining its meaning.

rituals.title: REGRET HAS TWO DIRECTIONS
rituals.targetPattern: Imagined regret dominated by visible action
rituals.target_pattern: Imagined regret dominated by visible action
rituals.precise_subpattern: Imagined regret dominated by visible action
rituals.vibeLine: Funny how “do nothing” was pretending it had no sequel.
rituals.hook: Regret keeps showing you one direction.
rituals.predict: Guess which regret feels louder: doing the thing and disliking it, or never testing it at all.
rituals.play: Create two ten-second future scenes: “I tried and it was wrong for me,” then “I never tried and still wonder.” Don’t choose yet; just compare the emotional texture.
rituals.catch: Check if your mind had been simulating only one kind of regret.
rituals.reveal: Avoidance often protects us from visible regret while hiding invisible regret.
rituals.mindBend: Not acting is also a decision with a future.

rituals.mindBend: A choice can be true for now without becoming a lifelong autobiography.

unfiltered.predict: Guess whether the decision feels easier if it is allowed to mean only “for now.”
unfiltered.play: Take the choice and append: “for the next 30 days” or another realistic review window. Imagine revisiting it then with new information.
unfiltered.catch: Check if identity pressure falls when permanence is removed.
unfiltered.reveal: Many decisions are revisable, but the mind upgrades them into identity declarations.
unfiltered.mindBend: A choice can be true for now without becoming a lifelong autobiography.
unfiltered.safety:
PAUSE
Keep the example you picked within an ordinary safe task. A micro-step should reduce friction, not bypass limits, needed rest or a high-stakes decision process. The result is a working perspective, not proof that the opposite story is true.
unfiltered.targetPattern: A decision treated as permanent self-definition
unfiltered.mechanismFingerprint: Convert a perceived identity-defining decision into a time-bounded reversible commitment with an explicit review point.

rituals.target_pattern: Claimed priorities mismatching actual calendar
rituals.precise_subpattern: Claimed priorities mismatching actual calendar
rituals.vibeLine: Your values memo and your diary may need a meeting.
rituals.hook: Your calendar may know what your mouth keeps saying matters.
rituals.predict: Guess which value gets the most actual minutes this week.
rituals.play: Pick one stated priority. Scan the last seven days for concrete time spent on it—minutes count. No guilt, just data.
rituals.catch: Compare stated importance with behavioural evidence.
rituals.reveal: Values can be sincere and still lose every scheduling battle.
rituals.mindBend: What matters to you may need calendar space, not stronger feelings.

rituals.vibeLine: Strong people are apparently allowed lunch too.
rituals.hook: Even your favourite identity word can become a cage.
rituals.predict: Guess which label you work hardest to maintain: strong, nice, smart, reliable, calm, successful.
rituals.play: Choose one identity adjective. For 10 sec imagine you Don’t have to prove it today. Ask what action becomes available.
rituals.catch: Check if relief, fear or resistance appears.
rituals.reveal: Positive identities can create pressure when every behaviour must defend them.
rituals.mindBend: You can value a trait without auditioning for it all day.

unfiltered.play: Choose one identity adjective. For 10 sec imagine you Don’t have to prove it today. Ask what action becomes available.
unfiltered.catch: Check if relief, fear or resistance appears.
unfiltered.reveal: Positive identities can create pressure when every behaviour must defend them.
unfiltered.mindBend: You can value a trait without auditioning for it all day.
unfiltered.safety:
PAUSE
Use the chosen example to loosen a rigid story about yourself, not to deny real needs, responsibilities, discrimination, abuse or other concrete circumstances. Leave room for new evidence after the exercise instead of treating the result as final.
unfiltered.targetPattern: A chosen trait becoming a prison
unfiltered.mechanismFingerprint: Temporarily suspend the need to perform a valued identity adjective and observe newly available behaviour.

rituals.name: THE DOOR YOU CLOSE
rituals.title: THE DOOR YOU CLOSE
rituals.targetPattern: Every choice experienced only as what it gives, not what it closes
rituals.target_pattern: Every choice experienced only as what it gives, not what it closes
rituals.precise_subpattern: Every choice experienced only as what it gives, not what it closes
rituals.vibeLine: Commitment looks different when the receipt includes what you gave up.
rituals.hook: Every yes quietly closes something.
rituals.predict: Guess which loss you are pretending this choice does not contain.
rituals.play: For your preferred option, name one real thing it costs: time, flexibility, another path, money, comfort, identity, approval. Ask whether the yes is still worth that no.
rituals.catch: Notice how commitment feels when the cost is named rather than hidden.
rituals.reveal: Choice becomes cleaner when both gain and sacrifice are allowed into the room.
rituals.mindBend: A meaningful yes usually contains a real no.

rituals.name: WHO SIGNED THIS?
rituals.title: WHO SIGNED THIS?
rituals.targetPattern: Rules obeyed without current endorsement
rituals.target_pattern: Rules obeyed without current endorsement
rituals.precise_subpattern: Rules obeyed without current endorsement
rituals.vibeLine: Your inner voice may be quoting someone without citation.
rituals.hook: There is a rule in your head.
rituals.predict: Guess who originally taught, rewarded or modelled it.
rituals.play: Finish: “A good person should ___.” Then add: “According to ___.” If the source is vague, write CULTURE / FAMILY / OLD ME / UNKNOWN.
rituals.catch: Check if the rule feels different once authorship appears.
rituals.reveal: Internalised rules often feel self-authored after their source is forgotten.
rituals.mindBend: A rule can live in your voice without having been chosen by you.

rituals.vibeLine: Maybe the title was just a middleman.
rituals.hook: The trophy may be standing in for something else.

rituals.vibeLine: Leaving 20% in the tank is not a criminal offence.
rituals.hook: Enough is a line you can choose before everything is exhausted.

rituals.reveal: Without a chosen stopping rule, achievement expands to consume available effort.
rituals.mindBend: Enough is not what remains after you are empty.

rituals.vibeLine: No points. No badge. Still worth doing?
rituals.hook: What would you still do if none of it could be counted?
rituals.predict: Guess which activity survives when hours, streaks, steps, tasks and output disappear.
rituals.play: Imagine your tracking apps and to-do ticks vanish for a day. Pick one thing you would still choose because of the experience or consequence itself.
rituals.catch: Notice which motivation remains without measurement.
rituals.reveal: Measurement can support action and quietly become the reason for action.
rituals.mindBend: A metric can track meaning without manufacturing it.

rituals.name: THE UNSIGNED PERMISSION SLIP
rituals.title: THE UNSIGNED PERMISSION SLIP
rituals.targetPattern: Waiting for external approval to make a benign personal choice
rituals.target_pattern: Waiting for external approval to make a benign personal choice
rituals.precise_subpattern: Waiting for external approval to make a benign personal choice
rituals.vibeLine: Wild concept: no committee required.
rituals.hook: This harmless choice is waiting for a signature that may not exist.
rituals.predict: Guess whose approval you imagine needing.
rituals.play: Name one low-stakes personal choice. Write an imaginary permission slip and leave the signature line blank. Read: “Permission granted by: nobody required.”
rituals.catch: Notice the discomfort of acting without an approving authority.
rituals.reveal: Some choices feel forbidden only because approval became habitual.
rituals.mindBend: Autonomy can feel like rule-breaking when you are used to asking.

rituals.name: WHO HANDED YOU THAT SCRIPT?
rituals.title: WHO HANDED YOU THAT SCRIPT?
rituals.targetPattern: A family or cultural script treated as self-chosen identity
rituals.target_pattern: A family or cultural script treated as self-chosen identity
rituals.precise_subpattern: A family or cultural script treated as self-chosen identity
rituals.vibeLine: Just because the rule came preinstalled does not mean updates are banned.
rituals.hook: Some life scripts arrive before we can read.
rituals.predict: Guess which rule about success, family, work, love, or respect came from somewhere else first.
rituals.play: Finish: “A good person is supposed to ___.” Then ask who taught that rule, directly or indirectly. Finally ask: “Would I choose it if I met it today?”
rituals.catch: Notice the difference between inherited familiarity and current endorsement.
rituals.reveal: A belief can be deeply yours in history without being yours by choice.
rituals.mindBend: You are allowed to audit the script you inherited.

unfiltered.play: Name the domain hurting most. Name four others—health, family, friendship, work, money, home, play, learning, body, rest—and give each a one-word status.
unfiltered.catch: Check if your total-life verdict changes when the other rooms reappear.
unfiltered.reveal: Whatever we focus on feels disproportionately important to overall wellbeing.
unfiltered.mindBend: A bad room can need attention without becoming the whole house.
unfiltered.moveOn: ↻ ONE ROOM IS NOT THE HOUSE
unfiltered.safety:
PAUSE
Keep the naming step to one brief experiment. If it starts making you less steady, more confused or more stuck, stop and return to the concrete facts in front of you. The result is a working perspective, not proof that the opposite story is true.
unfiltered.returnPrompt: ↻ ONE ROOM IS NOT THE HOUSE
unfiltered.targetPattern: One life domain dominating overall life evaluation
unfiltered.theoryBackbone: Focusing illusion; life satisfaction; attentional salience
unfiltered.mechanismFingerprint: Expand a global life evaluation from one salient domain to a multi-domain snapshot to reduce focus-induced over-weighting.

rituals.name: THE MIDDLE WANTS A VOTE
rituals.title: THE MIDDLE WANTS A VOTE
rituals.targetPattern: Whole period judged mainly by its worst moment and ending
rituals.target_pattern: Whole period judged mainly by its worst moment and ending
rituals.precise_subpattern: Whole period judged mainly by its worst moment and ending
rituals.vibeLine: Peak and ending were hogging the review panel.
rituals.hook: Your memory invited the peak and the ending.
rituals.predict: Guess whether your verdict changes when you sample three ordinary middle moments too.
rituals.play: Pick the period you are judging. Name its worst point, its ending, and three middle moments that were neutral, useful, funny, calm, or simply uneventful.
rituals.catch: Check if the overall memory becomes less cinematic and more textured.
rituals.reveal: We often remember episodes disproportionately through their peak and ending.
rituals.mindBend: The middle may be boring, but boring is part of the truth.

rituals.displayName: WHAT ARE YOU BUYING WITH THE NO?

rituals.mindBend: A no is not empty. It is a transfer.

Take one thing you may decline. Write two columns: “I lose…” and “I buy…” Include time, energy, focus, peace, money, opportunity, identity, connection.
Guess what your refusal creates room for.
Check if the no still feels like pure loss once the purchased space is visible. Declining one option reallocates scarce resources to another.
↻ WHAT ARE YOU BUYING WITH THE NO?

rituals.name: EMPTY ROOM DECISION
rituals.title: EMPTY ROOM DECISION
rituals.targetPattern: Wanting something because it is expected in the group
rituals.target_pattern: Wanting something because it is expected in the group
rituals.precise_subpattern: Wanting something because it is expected in the group
rituals.vibeLine: No audience, no status points, no family group chat. Interesting.
rituals.hook: Take the group out of the room and see what remains.
rituals.predict: Guess whether your choice changes if nobody you know can ever compare it with theirs.
rituals.play: Imagine making the decision in a world where friends, family and colleagues will never know the answer. What do you choose there?
rituals.catch: Notice which preference strengthens, weakens, or becomes quieter.
rituals.reveal: Social norms can shape desire before we experience them as pressure.
rituals.mindBend: Privacy is a useful laboratory for finding your own preference.

rituals.name: DELETE THREE GOOD OPTIONS
rituals.title: DELETE THREE GOOD OPTIONS
rituals.targetPattern: More options mistaken for more freedom
rituals.target_pattern: More options mistaken for more freedom
rituals.precise_subpattern: More options mistaken for more freedom
rituals.vibeLine: You do not need to keep every decent option on life support.
rituals.hook: Freedom can become homework when every decent option stays alive.
rituals.predict: Guess whether you feel lighter or trapped after temporarily deleting three acceptable choices.
rituals.play: Pick three options that are genuinely fine but not your current favourite. Mark them “closed for today.” Leave only the top two in active consideration.
rituals.catch: Check if loss or relief arrives first.
rituals.reveal: Keeping every option open has a cognitive cost.
rituals.mindBend: Freedom is not the number of doors you refuse to close.

rituals.name: IF NOBODY COULD FORCE YOU
rituals.title: IF NOBODY COULD FORCE YOU
rituals.targetPattern: A goal pursued mainly because resistance feels forbidden
rituals.target_pattern: A goal pursued mainly because resistance feels forbidden
rituals.precise_subpattern: A goal pursued mainly because resistance feels forbidden
rituals.vibeLine: No one is forcing you. Interesting what remains.
rituals.hook: Take pressure out of the room for ten seconds.
rituals.predict: Guess whether you would still choose the goal if saying no had zero social cost.
rituals.play: Imagine everyone affected would calmly accept either answer. Under that impossible freedom, what do you want?
rituals.catch: Notice what becomes audible when rebellion and compliance both lose their audience.
rituals.reveal: Pressure can blur preference in both directions.
rituals.mindBend: Freedom is useful not because you always say no, but because it lets a real yes appear.
rituals.ritualCard:
Take pressure out of the room for ten seconds.
Imagine everyone affected would calmly accept either answer. Under that impossible freedom, what do you want?
Guess whether you would still choose the goal if saying no had zero social cost.
Notice what becomes audible when rebellion and compliance both lose their audience. Pressure can blur preference in both directions.

rituals.name: ENVY IS AN X-RAY
rituals.title: ENVY IS AN X-RAY
rituals.targetPattern: Social comparison hiding a specific desired quality
rituals.target_pattern: Social comparison hiding a specific desired quality
rituals.precise_subpattern: Social comparison hiding a specific desired quality
rituals.vibeLine: Their whole life was never the assignment.
rituals.hook: Envy may be pointing at one feature, not asking you to become the whole person.
rituals.predict: Guess the exact thing you envy: freedom, skill, attention, money, confidence, beauty, time, belonging, courage.
rituals.play: Take the person out of the picture. Keep only the quality. Ask what tiny version of that quality could exist in your life this month.
rituals.catch: Check if envy becomes directional rather than personal.
rituals.reveal: Comparison can reveal unmet values when the person is separated from the feature.
rituals.mindBend: You may not want their life. You may want one ingredient.

rituals.title: NEW DOESN’T MEAN FAKE
rituals.targetPattern: Unfamiliar behaviour mistaken for being fake or inauthentic
rituals.target_pattern: Unfamiliar behaviour mistaken for being fake or inauthentic
rituals.precise_subpattern: Unfamiliar behaviour mistaken for being fake or inauthentic
rituals.vibeLine: Awkward is not evidence of fraud.
rituals.hook: A new behaviour can feel fake simply because your nervous system has no rehearsal history.
rituals.predict: Guess which feels more 'authentic': the habit you have practised for years or the value you are only starting to practise.
rituals.play: Name 1 behaviour that fits who you want to be but feels awkward: speaking up, resting, saying no, accepting praise, being warm. Imagine doing it ten times.
rituals.catch: Check if 'fake' starts to look like 'unfamiliar.'
rituals.reveal: Familiarity contributes to the feeling of authenticity.
rituals.mindBend: You can be sincere before a new behaviour feels natural.

rituals.targetPattern: Growth confused with achievement rather than new capacities and experiences
rituals.target_pattern: Growth confused with achievement rather than new capacities and experiences
rituals.precise_subpattern: Growth confused with achievement rather than new capacities and experiences
rituals.vibeLine: Growth does not always need a leaderboard.
rituals.hook: Growth is not only climbing.
rituals.predict: Guess which experience would expand what you can do, notice, understand, or enjoy.
rituals.play: Choose one small expansion: talk to someone new, learn a tool, visit a place, try a cuisine, ask a question, make something badly.
rituals.catch: Notice how this differs from proving competence.
rituals.reveal: Novel experiences can expand self-concept without needing status or mastery.
rituals.mindBend: A bigger life is not always a higher score.
rituals.ritualCard:
Growth is not only climbing.
Choose one small expansion: talk to someone new, learn a tool, visit a place, try a cuisine, ask a question, make something badly.

Notice how this differs from proving competence. Novel experiences can expand self-concept without needing status or mastery.

rituals.name: THREE FUTURE AUDITIONS
rituals.title: THREE FUTURE AUDITIONS
rituals.targetPattern: One feared future crowding out alternative futures
rituals.target_pattern: One feared future crowding out alternative futures
rituals.precise_subpattern: One feared future crowding out alternative futures
rituals.vibeLine: Your worst-case actor was getting way too many scenes.
rituals.hook: Your brain cast one future and cancelled auditions.
rituals.predict: Guess two different future versions of you that could also plausibly exist.
rituals.play: For the same time point, sketch three futures: feared, ordinary, unexpectedly good. Give each one mundane details, not fantasy.
rituals.catch: Notice how the future stops behaving like a single pre-recorded film.
rituals.reveal: Imagined futures are possibilities, not memories waiting to happen.
rituals.mindBend: One vivid future does not own the casting rights.
rituals.ritualCard:
Your brain cast one future and cancelled auditions.
For the same time point, sketch three futures: feared, ordinary, unexpectedly good. Give each one mundane details, not fantasy.
Guess two different future versions of you that could also plausibly exist.
Notice how the future stops behaving like a single pre-recorded film. Imagined futures are possibilities, not memories waiting to happen.
↻ THREE FUTURE AUDITIONS

rituals.name: GOOD VS GOOD
rituals.title: GOOD VS GOOD
rituals.targetPattern: Two good values competing and being misread as indecision
rituals.target_pattern: Two good values competing and being misread as indecision
rituals.precise_subpattern: Two good values competing and being misread as indecision
rituals.vibeLine: No villain. Very inconvenient.
rituals.hook: Sometimes you are stuck because both sides matter, not because you lack courage.
rituals.predict: Guess which two values are pulling against each other.
rituals.play: Name both without making either stupid: freedom vs security, honesty vs kindness, ambition vs rest, loyalty vs growth.
rituals.catch: Notice how the conflict changes when both sides are respected.
rituals.reveal: Hard choices often involve competing goods rather than good versus bad.
rituals.mindBend: Indecision can be evidence that two values are alive.

rituals.predict: Guess which feedback your brain accepts faster: familiar criticism or unfamiliar praise.

cheeky.predict: Guess how certain a genuinely good decision should realistically feel before its outcome exists.
cheeky.play: Think of one past decision that worked out well. Remember how much uncertainty you had before making it.
cheeky.catch: Check if good outcomes in your own history required perfect confidence.
cheeky.reveal: Decision quality and subjective certainty are only loosely linked.
cheeky.mindBend: A good choice can arrive wearing doubt.
cheeky.safety:
PAUSE
Keep the memory/imagery pass to one planned pass. Do not keep adding evidence until you feel perfectly certain; uncertainty is allowed to remain. Keep the result tied to this one example rather than generalising it to every situation.
cheeky.targetPattern: Belief that the correct path should feel fully certain
cheeky.theoryBackbone: Decision confidence; uncertainty tolerance; retrospective calibration
cheeky.mechanismFingerprint: Use a successful past decision with remembered pre-decision uncertainty as counterevidence to the rule that correct choices feel certain.

rituals.name: WHAT DISAPPEARED FROM VIEW?
rituals.title: WHAT DISAPPEARED FROM VIEW?
rituals.targetPattern: Limited resources narrowing attention to immediate deficits
rituals.target_pattern: Limited resources narrowing attention to immediate deficits
rituals.precise_subpattern: Limited resources narrowing attention to immediate deficits
rituals.vibeLine: Scarcity put one problem in IMAX and dimmed the rest.
rituals.hook: When one resource feels scarce, the mind can turn into a tunnel.
rituals.predict: Guess what important thing you stop noticing when time, money, attention, or energy feels tight.
rituals.play: Name the scarce resource. Deliberately name two long-term priorities that the shortage is pushing out of view.
rituals.catch: Notice the tunnel—not as failure, but as a predictable attentional effect.
rituals.reveal: Scarcity captures bandwidth and narrows planning.
rituals.mindBend: What feels urgent can become visible partly because everything else went dark.

rituals.reveal: Outcomes affect moral judgment even when control was identical.
rituals.mindBend: You can take responsibility for your choice without claiming authorship of every consequence.

rituals.name: ROLE EXIT RITUAL
rituals.title: ROLE EXIT RITUAL
rituals.targetPattern: A demanding role consuming identity outside its context
rituals.target_pattern: A demanding role consuming identity outside its context
rituals.precise_subpattern: A demanding role consuming identity outside its context
rituals.vibeLine: Badge off. Human remains.
rituals.hook: Some roles forget to leave when the shift ends.
rituals.predict: Guess what part of the role you are still carrying after its job is done.
rituals.play: At the transition out of the role, name one physical or symbolic action: close laptop, change clothes, put badge away, walk one block, say 'shift over.'
rituals.catch: Check if the role feels more bounded.
rituals.reveal: Transitions help separate role identities and reduce spillover.
rituals.mindBend: You can care about a role without making it your permanent operating system.

unfiltered.predict: Guess the event that most clearly marks 'before' and 'after.'
unfiltered.play: Name the old chapter in three words. Name the transition event. Name the current chapter in three different words.
unfiltered.catch: Check if old rules still feel automatically applicable.
unfiltered.reveal: Narrative chapter boundaries help organise identity change over time.
unfiltered.mindBend: A rule from chapter three may not belong in chapter seven.
unfiltered.safety:
PAUSE
Keep the naming step on the interpretation, not the other person's rights or limits. A kinder explanation does not cancel a clear no, repeated harm or needed distance. Leave room for new evidence after the exercise instead of treating the result as final.
unfiltered.targetPattern: Past identity treated as current because no chapter boundary was acknowledged
unfiltered.mechanismFingerprint: Create an explicit narrative boundary between a past identity period and the current period, then inspect whether old rules still fit.

rituals.name: TURN DOWN THE IDENTITY ZOOM
rituals.title: TURN DOWN THE IDENTITY ZOOM
rituals.targetPattern: Temporary crisis making one identity dimension consume the entire self
rituals.target_pattern: Temporary crisis making one identity dimension consume the entire self
rituals.precise_subpattern: Temporary crisis making one identity dimension consume the entire self
rituals.vibeLine: One role was occupying full-screen mode.
rituals.hook: The crisis is zoomed in so far that one identity has filled the whole screen.
rituals.predict: Guess which other parts of you are currently outside the frame.
rituals.play: Name the threatened identity, then list four identities that remain intact and relevant.
rituals.catch: Notice how the self becomes larger than the threatened role.
rituals.reveal: Identity centrality changes under stress and can narrow self-definition.
rituals.mindBend: A threatened part of you can be huge without becoming all of you.

KPI-free zone established.

Some joy dies from too much reporting.
cheeky.ritualCard:
Some joy dies from too much reporting.
Take one activity you value. Imagine one session with no tracking, output target, audience, or monetisable result.
Guess what the activity felt like before it had numbers, posting, targets, or monetisation.
Check if the activity changes category in your mind. Metrics can crowd out intrinsic motives and alter experienced meaning.

rituals.name: WHO WROTE THE TIMELINE?
rituals.title: WHO WROTE THE TIMELINE?
rituals.targetPattern: Personal preference judged against a social life-timeline script
rituals.target_pattern: Personal preference judged against a social life-timeline script
rituals.precise_subpattern: Personal preference judged against a social life-timeline script
rituals.vibeLine: Apparently adulthood came with an unofficial Gantt chart.
rituals.hook: A life milestone can feel late because somebody drew an invisible schedule.
rituals.predict: Guess the age or sequence you believe this 'should' happen by.
rituals.play: Write the timeline rule: 'By ___, people should ___.' Then ask where you learned it and whether it fits your actual circumstances and values.
rituals.catch: Notice how urgency changes when the script gains an author.
rituals.reveal: Cultural life scripts shape autobiographical expectations.
rituals.mindBend: A socially common timeline is not a law of human development.

rituals.targetPattern: A past failure feeling permanently self-defining despite psychological distance

rituals.precise_subpattern: A past failure feeling permanently self-defining despite psychological distance
rituals.vibeLine: Still your history. Not necessarily your current résumé.
rituals.hook: A past version of you may still be standing too close to the present.
rituals.predict: Guess whether the same old mistake feels different when you picture how many versions of you have existed since.
rituals.play: Place the event on a simple timeline. Add three meaningful changes that happened after it—skills, roles, knowledge, relationships, responsibilities, or choices.
rituals.catch: Check if the old event still feels equally representative of current-you.
rituals.reveal: Temporal distance changes how strongly past selves are assimilated into current identity.
rituals.mindBend: An old event can stay true while becoming less representative of who is standing here now.

rituals.name: YOU BUILT IT, SO CHECK THE PRICE
rituals.title: YOU BUILT IT, SO CHECK THE PRICE
rituals.ritual_name: YOU BUILT IT, SO CHECK THE PRICE
rituals.displayName: YOU BUILT IT, SO CHECK THE PRICE
rituals.targetPattern: Something feeling more valuable because one helped build or create it
rituals.target_pattern: Something feeling more valuable because one helped build or create it
rituals.precise_subpattern: Something feeling more valuable because one helped build or create it
rituals.vibeLine: You built it. That explains attachment, not perfection.
rituals.hook: Your effort can sneak into the valuation of what you made.
rituals.predict: Guess how you would rate the same rough result if somebody else created it.
rituals.play: Take something you made, planned, or assembled. Imagine it arrived anonymously from another person. Rate quality and usefulness again.
rituals.catch: Check if ownership-by-effort was adding value.
rituals.reveal: People often value self-created products more highly than equivalent externally created ones.
rituals.mindBend: Building something gives you attachment, not automatic quality.
rituals.moveOn: ↻ YOU BUILT IT, SO CHECK THE PRICE

HOOK

CATCH

REVEAL

MIND BEND

rituals.vibeLine: Same destination, different engine.
rituals.hook: The same goal can be powered by growth or protection.
rituals.predict: Guess which wording gives you more energy: 'gain X' or 'avoid losing Y.'

rituals.catch: Notice which frame fits the goal and your current motivation better.
rituals.reveal: Promotion and prevention focus orient attention toward different kinds of outcomes.
rituals.mindBend: Motivation changes when the same destination is described as advancement or protection.

rituals.vibeLine: Apparently 'always' has office hours.

Take one unavoidable task. Find one real choice still available: order, timing, location, method, pace, or who you involve.

Check if even a small ownership shift changes resistance. Autonomous choice supports motivation even when the broader obligation remains.
